1→# CoolStore Monolith
     2→
     3→This repository has the complete coolstore monolith built as a Java EE 7 application. To deploy it on JBoss 7.4 follow the instructions below
     4→
     5→
     6→## Pre requisite
     7→
     8→* JBoss 7.4 zip installation
     9→* Keycloak v20.0.5 zip installation
    10→* podman or docker, tested with podman version 4.3.1
    11→* maven, tested with maven version 3.8.5
    12→* OpenJDK, tested with version 17.0.5
    13→
    14→## Start a postgreSQL database
    15→
    16→```
    17→podman run --name myPostgresDb \
    18→   -p 5432:5432 \
    19→   -e POSTGRES_USER=postgresUser \
    20→   -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=postgresPW \
    21→   -e POSTGRES_DB=postgresDB \
    22→   -d postgres
    23→```
    24→
    25→## Start keycloak
    26→
    27→Extract keycloak-20.0.5.zip
    28→
    29→```cd keycloak-20.0.5```
    30→
    31→Start keycloak in dev mode listening on port 8081
    32→
    33→``` ./bin/kc.sh start-dev --http-port=8081 ```
    34→
    35→Open http://127.0.0.1:8081 in your browser
    36→
    37→
    38→Set an administrator username and password, then login to keycloak using these credentials
    39→
    40→Click on the "Master" dropdown, and select "Create Realm"
    41→
    42→Click on "Browse" and locate the file realm-export.json in this repo.
    43→
    44→Click on "Create" to create the "eap" realm
    45→
    46→Click on "Users" and "Create new user"
    47→
    48→Enter a username, e.g. "user1" and click on "Create"
    49→
    50→From the next form, click on the "Credentials" tab and "Set password"
    51→
    52→Set a password and password confirmation, and unselect "Temporary"
    53→
    54→Click on "Save" to store the password.
    55→
    56→Keycloak is now configured correctly
    57→
    58→## Configure JBoss 7.4
    59→
    60→Unzip jboss-eap-7.4.0.zip
    61→
    62→``` cd jboss-eap-7.4/jboss-eap-7.4 ```
    63→
    64→Create the folder modules/org/postgresql/main
    65→
    66→``` mkdir -p modules/org/postgresql/main ```
    67→
    68→
    69→Download the postgres jdbc driver from https://jdbc.postgresql.org/download/  e.g. https://jdbc.postgresql.org/download/postgresql-42.5.4.jar
    70→
    71→ Copy postgres jar file to modules/org/postgresql/main
    72→
    73→create module.xml  -- ensure the filename matches the filename downloaded in the previous step
    74→
    75→```
    76→cat <<EOF > modules/org/postgresql/main/module.xml
    77→<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
    78→<module xmlns="urn:jboss:module:1.0" name="org.postgresql">
    79→ <resources>
    80→ <resource-root path="postgresql-42.5.4.jar"/>
    81→ </resources>
    82→ <dependencies>
    83→ <module name="javax.api"/>
    84→ <module name="javax.transaction.api"/>
    85→ </dependencies>
    86→</module>
    87→EOF
    88→```
    89→
    90→
    91→Start JBoss EAP 7.4 in full high availability mode
    92→
    93→From the jboss-eap-7.4 folder run:
    94→
    95→```./jboss-eap-7.4-2/bin/standalone.sh -c standalone-full-ha.xml  -Djboss.node.name=node1 ```
    96→
    97→In another terminal, start the jboss cli, from the jboss7.4 installation folder run 
    98→
    99→```  ./bin/jboss-cli.sh --connect ```
   100→
   101→Run the following commands:
   102→
   103→```
   104→/subsystem=datasources/jdbc-driver=postgresql:add(driver-name=postgresql,driver-module-name=org.postgresql)
   105→```
   106→
   107→```
   108→ data-source add --name=CoolstoreDS --jndi-name=java:jboss/datasources/CoolstoreDS --driver-name=postgresql --connection-url=jdbc:postgresql://127.0.0.1:5432/postgresDB --user-name=postgresUser --password=postgresPW
   109→ ```
   110→
   111→```
   112→jms-topic add --topic-address=topic.orders --entries=topic/orders
   113→
   114→/subsystem=messaging-activemq/server=default:write-attribute(name=cluster-password, value=password)
   115→```
   116→
   117→## Build and deploy the application
   118→
   119→From the root of this repo, run: 
   120→
   121→`mvn package`
   122→
   123→Set the JBOSS_HOME env variable e.g. 
   124→
   125→`export JBOSS_HOME=~/jboss-eap-7.4/jboss-eap-7.4`
   126→
   127→Run the jboss cli: 
   128→
   129→` $JBOSS_HOME/bin/jboss-cli.sh`
   130→
   131→Run the following command to deploy the application:
   132→
   133→ `deploy ./target/ROOT.war`
   134→
   135→Navigate to http://127.0.0.1:8080
   136→
   137→![coolstore](assets/coolstore.png "coolstore")
   138→
   139→From the coostore, click on "Sign in" in the top right
   140→
   141→Login with the user credentials created on Keycloak, e.g. user1
   142→
   143→You should now be able to complete the checkout process.
   144→
   145→## Start a second instance.
   146→
   147→Make a copy of the jboss-eap-7.4/jboss-eap-7.4 e.g jboss-eap-7.4/jboss-eap-7.4-2
   148→
   149→Within the jboss-eap-7.4 folder you should now see jboss-eap-7.4 and jboss-eap-7.4-2
   150→
   151→In the jboss-eap-7.4-2, remove the contents of standalone/data/activemq
   152→
   153→From the jboss-eap-7.4 folder run:
   154→
   155→`./jboss-eap-7.4-2/bin/standalone.sh -c standalone-full-ha.xml -Djboss.socket.binding.port-offset=100  -Djboss.node.name=node2`
   156→
   157→## Monitor the logs
   158→
   159→Open up two terminals in the jboss-eap-7.4 folder
   160→
   161→Run:
   162→
   163→`tail -f jboss-eap-7.4/standalone/log/server.log` 
   164→
   165→in one terminal and 
   166→
   167→`tail -f jboss-eap-7.4-2/standalone/log/server.log` 
   168→
   169→in the other
   170→
   171→## Testing clustering
   172→
   173→If you perform a test checkout of an item, you should see both nodes processing the messages in the logs e.g.
   174→
   175→```
   176→2023-03-02 14:41:23,131 INFO  [stdout] (Thread-3 (ActiveMQ-client-global-threads)) 
   177→2023-03-02 14:41:23,131 INFO  [stdout] (Thread-3 (ActiveMQ-client-global-threads)) Message recd !
   178→2023-03-02 14:41:23,131 INFO  [stdout] (Thread-3 (ActiveMQ-client-global-threads)) Received order: {"orderValue":10.49,"customerName":"Karl Svensson","customerEmail":"karl@gmail.com","retailPrice":10.0,"discount":-2.5,"shippingFee":2.99,"shippingDiscount":0.0,"items":[{"productSku":"329299","quantity":1}]}
   179→2023-03-02 14:41:23,132 INFO  [stdout] (Thread-3 (ActiveMQ-client-global-threads)) Order object is Order [orderId=0, customerName=Karl Svensson, customerEmail=karl@gmail.com, orderValue=10.49, retailPrice=10.0, discount=-2.5, shippingFee=2.99, shippingDiscount=0.0, itemList=[OrderItem [productId=329299, quantity=1]]]
   180→
   181→
   182→```

**What's in the repo** — a Java EE 7 "CoolStore" monolith (README.md:1) deployed as a WAR on JBoss EAP 7.4, with an AngularJS frontend (`src/main/webapp/app/`), JPA/Postgres persistence via Flyway, JMS/ActiveMQ messaging, and Keycloak auth.

**Graph** — 1022 nodes / 2523 edges across 53 files: 259 functions, 95 classes, 47 annotations, 82 modules, 196 imports, 10 dependencies. Key edges: `contains` 946, `definedin` 969, `uses` 196, `calls` 138, `references` 62, `instantiates` 28, `implements` 14, `extends` 2.

**Stack signals** — imports are heavily `javax.*` (persistence, ws, ejb, inject, jms, enterprise), plus `com.redhat` (33). Maven deps include `javax:javaee-api:7.0` and `flyway-core:4.1.2` (pom.xml).

**Structure** — named communities: ShoppingCart (35), `redhat.coolstore` (31), `coolstore.model::ToJson` (28), `coolstore.service::Entity` (19). Pagerank hotspots: `login`/`logout` (controllers.js), `getCart` (cart.js), `checkout`, and `CatalogItemEntity`.

**Capabilities** — structural graph and semantic index ready; CFG/CPG not built (run `discover --with-cfg` if you need slicing/mutations).

events.text:
I checked first, and this doesn't look like a two-service monorepo. There's exactly one build descriptor — `pom.xml` — producing a single WAR; `src/main/java` holds one app (`com.redhat.coolstore` + `weblogic` stubs), and the "frontend" is bundled AngularJS static assets under `src/main/webapp/bower_components/`, not a separately deployable service. No second `pom.xml`, `build.gradle`, `Dockerfile`, or `docker-compose`. So nothing to merge here — one `discover` already unifies it.

If you do have two distinct service roots, the workflow is:

- Index each root separately: `rgctl -r svcA discover .` and `rgctl -r svcB discover .` (each writes its own `.rgctl/graph.snapshot.bin`)
- Merge the snapshots: `rgctl merge svcA svcB --output-dir merged`
- Query the merged artifact: `rgctl -r merged -f json inventory --by type`, then `blast-radius`/`callers` across service boundaries

Practical notes: apply each service's own `-e` excludes during discover; watch for duplicate fully-qualified class names across services (e.g. shared DTOs) which can collide in the merged graph; and `merge` combines outputs, not live working trees.

Want me to point it at specific sibling roots if the second service lives elsewhere?
